data.exact_reserve_text: The 2017 calendar year GAAP result is a loss of $2.6 million (combined ratio 100.8%). This consists of profits of $2.7 million and $0.6 million on the 2015 and prior and 2016 years of account respectively, while the 2017 year of account produced a calendar year loss of $5.9 million.

data.standardized_narrative: At the 2017 year end Syndicate 3010 opened with gross claims outstanding of 51.924m (USD). The syndicate reports a net prior-year release of approximately 3.299m (USD) driven by favourable development on prior years (profits of $2.7m on 2015 & prior and $0.6m on 2016). No material adverse prior-year reserve movements were reported; closed years 2007-2014 produced a surplus. 2017 catastrophe activity (Harvey/Irma/Maria and Californian wildfires) is expected to have a modest aggregate impact (~$3.5m).
raw_causal_phrases: There were no issues arising from our closed years (2007 to 2014) and all of these years combined produced a surplus which contributed both to the calendar year result and the closing 2015 account result.
It is pleasing that all classes, including those in startup, have made positive contributions to the Underwriting Balance.
This result for Energy includes exposure on the Ghanaian Jubilee oil field loss, the largest man-made loss for 2016.

The anticipated aggregate losses emanating from the series of unusually severe natural catastrophe events are small and anticipated to be less than $3.5m ($2m from Hurricanes Harvey Irma and Maria combined and $1.5m from Californian wildfires).

data.data_quality_notes: All amounts are taken from the syndicate financial statements presented in US Dollars and returned in millions (USD). The prior-year development figure is derived from the reported year-of-account breakdown (profits of $2.7m and $0.6m for 2015 & prior and 2016 respectively) rather than a standalone 'movement in prior year provision' gross reconciliation. No absolute gross claims development triangle in currency amounts was provided; a loss-ratio development table is present instead.
